newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen easing to 123 after Sakakibara comments.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen easing to 123 after Sakakibara comments.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are expected to fall on Monday with 123.00 in sight, traders said.

Sentiment worsened after Friday's Tokyo close at 123.64 after senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara was quoted as telling Le Monde that a rise in Japan's discount rate to 1.0 percent is expected in the coming year, traders said.

"I don't think that the Bank of Japan will raise its discount rate before it is sure of a solid economic upturn," Sakakibara was quoted as saying. "But the monetary tightening should not have a major impact on the economic recovery."
"The discount rate is currently very low. If it rises by 0.5 percent, it will be at 1.0 percent, which remains low. A move on such a scale should be expected in the coming year," Sakakibara said.

"Sakakibara's remark can be interpreted in two ways: a Japanese credit tightening is not coming so soon, or it will definitely come in the coming year," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
"Either way, the remark was not surprising to many operators. But they may have to respect such a comment and try a downside."

Traders said the June may find a floor just above 123.00, underpinned by continued rolling over of short positions to the September contract by dealers ahead of a shift in benchmark status in early June.
If the June breaks through below 123.00, it may fall to a recent low of 122.70, they said.
